{{short description|Mathematical conjecture}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[algebraic K-theory]], the '''Birch–Tate conjecture''' is a [[conjecture]] proposed by [[Bryan John Birch]] and [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]] relating the <math>K_2</math> group of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] to its [[Dedekind zeta function]].

==Statement==
Formally, the [[group (mathematics)|group]] <math>K_2</math> of a [[number field]] <math>F</math> is defined as the [[Center (group theory)|center]] of the [[Steinberg group (K-theory)|Steinberg group]] of the [[ring of integers]] of <math>F</math>. <math>K_2</math> is also known as the tame kernel of <math>F</math>. The Birch–Tate conjecture relates the [[Order (group theory)|order]] of this group (its number of elements) to the value of the [[Dedekind zeta function]] <math>\zeta_F</math>.

More specifically, let <math>F</math> be a [[totally real number field]] and let <math>N</math> be the largest [[positive integer]] such that the [[Field extension|extension]] of <math>F</math> by the <math>N</math>-th [[root of unity]] has an [[Elementary abelian group|elementary abelian]] [[p-group|2-group]] as its [[Galois group]]. Then the conjecture states that
:<math>\#K_2 = |N\cdot\zeta_F(-1)|.</math>

==Status==
Progress on this conjecture has been made as a consequence of work on [[Iwasawa theory]], and in particular of the proofs given for the so-called "[[main conjecture of Iwasawa theory]]."
